Rega remarkable script purports to be produced under the direct inspiration of Apollonius of Tyana. Apollonius was almosta contemporaryof Christ, though according to his biographer Philostratus he lived to be more than a hundred years old, dying in the reign of Nerva. He had the reputation of being the greatest philosopher and thaumaturgist of his age. That being so, one would imagine that the difference would be clear if anEnglish lady, perfectly ignorant of philosophy or of Apollonius, were to take his place, especially as her script is written off without pause or emendation. I venture to say that there is no such difference, and that this contribution to human knowledge is in all ways worthy of one of the greatest minds that ever functioned upon earth. Of course, it would be easy to pick a sentence here or a sentence there which would make such criticism seem exaggerated, but I am alluding to the massive general effect of the book—an effect so lofty that it would take a considerable contemporary brain to appreciate it fully. Yet Apollonius is conscious that it falls short of his true knowledge, and he says, *“* T cannot pour the eternal wisdom of the Cosmos into a vessel of flesh and blood, but, as I am enabled, thus do.’ The book can, I think, stand or fall on its own

internal evidence of authorship. We may fairly ask, “* Tf it is impossible that this scribe really wrote it, then who did?” Vague talk of the subconscious self will not help us. There is the document. Does it correspond with the alleged author, or is it the unaided work of an English lady? There is, I am told, some extraneous corroboration, messages received independently through other mediums. But the book itself is its own best proof of a high external inspiration. FEEL that, in seeking publicity for this small volume of inspirational script, it is necessary to insert a short account of its inception, and of my own small part in its achievement. No planchette or ouija-board has been used in the production of this Writing. It has come to me clairaudiently, each word faint, yet distinct, within the mind as is the memory of notes which comprise a tune. As a rule, the language has flowed fluently, without pause or interruption, and with such rapidity that it has taxed my clerical powers to the utmost. At other times, the sentences have come word by word, with appreciable pauses, so that it has been impossible to follow the sense of the context until the whole paragraph could be read over. The New Nuctemeron took six weeks to complete. I wrote about five days each week, between ten-thirty in the morning and midday. The onlylight allowed me was a small red lamp. With regard to the identity of the Control under whose influence I have worked, I do not wish, even now, to be dogmatic. He came to me after I had been engaged in psychic writing for about a year, and gave me his name as “ Arcazaiel.” I was definitely aware of 7 Bo

his presence, and of an influence which differed in many ways from that exerted by my previous Guides. During the first pages of our work, he referred repeatedly to Apollonius of Tyana, who was then scarcely more than a name to me, and these references were so intimate in nature that I began to realize that he spoke thus of himself. There may be others who, like myself, are somewhat prejudiced against the use of great names in the séance-room, for the reasons, firstly, that they savour somewhat of sensationalism, and, secondly, because their use has been abused. For these, I think, my Guide desires to remain incognito under the pseudonym of “ Arcazaiel.” I cannot leave this subject without reference to that other Control who has assisted in the production of this book. I refer to Zabdiel, whose name will be familiar to all readers of the Vale-Owen Script. It was under his guidance I received my first Writings, and my most profound gratitude is due to Mr. Vale Owen for his kindness in establishing the accuracy of these messages, and the identity of the Guide. Had it not been for his sympathy at this juncture, the work would have progressed no further, for it requires the utmost faith to believe oneself to be a Medium, and, at the outset, I was only too ready to receive other and more material explanations of the phenomena accorded me. I wish also to express my most grateful thanks to Sir Arthur Conan Doyle and also to the Reverend Doctor Lamond for their unfailing sympathy and 8

encouragement, as well as for their confidence in a true source of inspiration which has given me the courage to bring this work before the public. I do this now with great diffidence, knowing only too well that in many passages I have been a bad scribe, and that I have obstructed, or modified, and even distorted, the flow of wisdom poured into my dull ears. My present hope is that this volume may reach one or two whose hearts, like mine, have sought for Truth, and that they may be comforted and enlightened as I have been. Marjorie LivincsTon.

He sees around him a mass of living matter, functioning variously, he sees the heavenly bodies running their course, he is aware of his own body obeying the impulse of his brain, and of his mind reaching out toward a comprehension of these things. He would go further than this. He would analyse the Life-Essences, he would penetrate into the Mysteries of the Creative Principles, he would approach in all reverence, God’s Book of Natural Law. This is the natural function of Man, it is thus and thus only he aspires to Nirvana. I am here speaking of your world as a phase of existence, there are few who undertake the studies of the Neophyte whilst in this state of progression. Nevertheless, the work is on the intellectual plane and is fitted to the conditions of terrene existence since Man therein receives a material brain through which his mental powers may function and which is well able to deal with the phenomenon of Matter. We are herein concerned with the descent of Spirit into Matter, and the return of Matter to the Spirit. In the beginning, God. The Story of the emanation of the Life-Spirit from God and of its descent through the Heavens is unattainable to mortals and is contained in the Mysteries which shall not be revealed until Man has ascended into these Spheres whence belong the unfoldments of the History of the Ages. What Angel-Forms the LifeSpark of God first animated, we may not know, or how it became debased, but we read of an Angel who strove to breast the current of Divine Love, and thus is revealed one aspect of the descent of Spirit.

It is of late that Man has learned there is no integral solidity in matter, and thereby he achieves the knowledge that matter is a production of the functioning of Spirit. All matter is a formation of Atoms which have attracted their affinities by their magnetic qualities—which latter also are Spirit-attributes— held in contact by cohesive force. In every analysis of matter, in every analysis of the Atom, man must come back to the elementals of all creation, which so far as he is able to penetrate, are electricity, magnetism, force, all of which are variations of the action of the
Life-Essence.

The alchemist shall evolve his potions from elementals which he may transmute and combine. He does not create. He does not add one iota to the actual weight liquefy and mass of the gases, or distil substances he uses. He may his liquids, but the atomic value of his concoctions remains unchanged.

A compact mass of matter will offer resistance to man’s physical body because that body in itself is another compact mass of Matter of independent substance, but similar density. Each is held together by its cohesive force, and will yield only to a force more powerful than itself. Nevertheless, there is no physical mass that can offer resistance to the LifeEssences. These are the forces which assembled the Atoms and which are withdrawn from Matter, but not destroyed. The vital Force which binds Man or Matter, physically, can be attracted towards its Source. In this event, death ensues in the case of a man, and disintegration in the case of Matter. Now, this Life-Essence, emanated from God, is actively conscious. Once you have established this fact scientifically, you will have no further ado in believing in individual consciousness surviving the disintegration of physical Atoms which men call death. First, there is the Consciousness of God, which we do not understand since we cannot conceive even the Idea of a Being so Exalted, Supreme, Eternal. Then, we know of cosmic consciousness, but we do not realize it, it is beyond the compass of our minds, but we know that a vital Force, emanating from the Creator, in itself creative and, I repeat, actively conscious, animates every electron, every Atom, every phase of existence not only in the earth planet and in the Universe in which it revolves, not only in the great visible cosmic arcana of the heavens, but also throughout all ethereal and spiritual existence which is normally Sh completely invisible to man for the simple reason that his physical body is furnished with no organs that are able to apprehend it. We come thus to individualized consciousness, normal and sub-normal. ‘The sub-, or more truly, the super-normal, is that section of individual consciousness which is aware of its connection with its affinity, with the cosmic and the Divine, and is therefore unable to function fully in the physical body of the individual for the reason but now set down, viz. the physical brain is not endowed with a capacity for its inclusion. This phase of individual consciousness is not affected by death, and may remain individualized through ages of existence, or it may, at the dictates of Free-will, become absorbed into cosmic and divine Consciousness which is the Ultimate Ecstasy. The restricted and active consciousness which animates the brain of physical man is that part of his vital Ego which his terrene structure is able to contain, and which functions in daily life by drawing on one hand upon the inexhaustible supply of power and inspiration which is in the subconscious, and on the other, registering every thought and experience which is undergone by the physical man. The Mind—that is the Riddle of the Ages, the Riddle of the Sphinx, for which the Initiate has descended beneath the arms of the Sphinx that he may discover in self-denial and torture, in silence and abnegation, the absolute solution. The Mind of Man is God. The Mind of Man is a spark sprung from the Godhead and descended through

infinities of space, modified, vitiated, incarnated in spirit-substance, and finally incarnated in flesh, yet still God. That is the Absolute Solution, but it is not to be received into comprehension by hearsay, it is a conviction to be achieved by such as are willing to undergo the trials by which the supreme knowledge is come at. I speak here of the gamut of human conceptions, the utmost limits of the scope of human intellect. We know not when the human element shall become eliminated. Spirit descended into Matter and a human race is one of the many results of this divine phenomenon, but when humanity shall have completed the Cycle and attained the sublimities of Spirit is beyond our power to know, and we are content to leave such knowledge with God, the Supreme, the Omniscient to Whom be all Glory, all praise, all honour now and throughout the Infinity of Ages which is the To-morrow of Creation. Amen. The first purpose, therefore, of the Neophyte is to discover the Divine within himself. He must learn to’ distinguish the Essences within his own Ego, since each individual stands as the representative of all. If he would know Mankind, he must know himself. It cannot in this condition, amalgamate with spirit-entities, since these are more complete in their development, and have through experience, acquired minds and intelligent consciousness. It is, therefore, obvious that its descent into Matter is not complete, its downward motion is as essential to its continued existence as its upward course must be. The Ego, therefore, conscious, but not, humanly speaking, intelligent, divine in its Source, but already modified by the elements which it has acquired for operation, seeks incarnation into a physical body. At this point, being ethereal in outer substance, Matter is no bar to its progress, and it is able to animate the Essences produced in protoplasm by parental humanity, and it therefore sets itself actively to acquire the physical elements necessary for its birth into existence on the earth planet. Therefore, truly God created visible man out of physical Matter, the dust of the Earth, and most truly was he also in God’s own Image, since it was the action of the animating Life-Spark, come from God, which was enabled to vivify that which would otherwise have been immobile. The descent of Matter itself from the Divine Essences to the physical compositions of Earth, I will, if permitted, deal with elsewhere, as I will also with the descent and incarnation of a Spirit into other realms and planets and into other states of existence. I am here concerned with conscious life as Man knows it and I wish to emphasize the fact that each unit of mankind must complete the Cycle of Existence before he can have fulfilled his destiny.

UCH inspired wisdom has been given to the Earth, and the Earth has been careless of its treasure. ‘Those of the present generation suffer for the wanton acts of the foolish and the ignorant of past decades. It is our will gradually to replace that which has been lost. There have been examples already of this work among you, and those of us who lived and wrote at a time when the intellect was well esteemed among you, are desirous now, out of our fuller knowledge, to write again that this means of wisdom may not be lacking at this period when the desire for gain has left mankind with little leisure for the pursuit of the true wisdom. The first manner in which a man becomes aware of himself as an entity, is through the physical. He experiences the sensations of his physical body and registers them in his carnate brain. For a while, he has no consciousness outside of Matter. Ignorant of the Source of his life, and of his spiritual status, 26

he identifies himself with the interests of the flesh, and the scope of his mind is encompassed by that which his brain-can accommodate. His descent into Matter is complete. Then, with the first overpowering emotion, the first inspiration from beyond the realm of flesh, cometh the first conscious stirring of the God within him. Not that which he is taught outwardly shall convince him. He may be told that his life shall outlast his body of flesh, that there is a Heaven and a Hell beyond the scope of his sight, where the just man shall be rewarded and the wicked endure the consequences of his misdeeds. But the Neophyte shall not be convinced thereby. His carnate brain may weigh and accept these partial truths, and his passage through Matter may be assisted by this moral support, but it is not thus he will gain his conquest over Matter or his vision of the true Nirvana. It is within himself that the Neophyte first must seek. It is within the Essences of his own identity that he will discover his divine origin and inheritance. It is only thus he can know himself as an integral part of the Cosmos, an entity in the process of development, passing in his present state through a phase analogous to the larve of an insect. What shall it know of flight _ by hearsay, this unwieldy segment of Matter? It must feel the stirring of its wings within the carcase of its own body. _ Herein, finding himself of God, the Neophyte shall encounter the forces of opposition. He will become aware of Evil, not only outwardly, but as a potentiality within himself. Now the force of Evil is a condition of Opposition. The Will of God, so far as we, humbly, may aspire to comprehend even one Aspect of It, works in a Cycle, carrying Spirit into the realm of Matter, there to incarnate, and drawing it again upward into the Region of Eternal Bliss. It is our belief the Cycle may be fashioned spiral-wise, so that there be no finality to man’s progress, no limits to his supernal joys. Now, I have made it clear hitherto that Man possesses this divine Force within himself, and that this same power permeates Creation and is in itself the potent factor which we call Life. This Force, therefore, individualized, is able to oppose itself to the main stream of Force which works progressively in a Cycle, and is known to men as God’s Love. It is this fact of opposition which reacts upon him much as would the contact of two opposing electrical forces. He causes a state of perversion, not only within his spiritual organism, but in the ether in his environment and within the minds of his fellow-men. ‘The alchemist is familiar with the results obtained from the admixture of antipathetic ingredients, the results of a clash of essences. The results are not less disasterous when Man, to put the matter in the simplest words, opposes his will to God’s. Beset about with Evil, therefore, pertaining to the Matter into which he was born, the Neophyte is at pains to discover in his own Being the trend of the Divine Essences, and to identify his nature and desires

with the Eternal Current. He may not exalt his body or pander to its lusts, for the adulation of Matter is retrogressive, and therefore is an action contrary to Progress. He may not indulge in cruelty and selfishness, because the Life-Stream of God is based on the principle of Attraction, and is a manifestation of Love. He must learn that the treasures of the world, the adulation of the multitude, the gain and the profit in material affairs, all appertain to Matter, and as such are valueless, and, in excess, retrogressive. In our day, upon the Earth planet, we emphasized our belief to such extent that we voluntarily mortified the body and despised Matter in allits forms. I counsel you not to do likewise, for we know now that Matter also, is His creation, though unprogressed in condition, and that the physical body is given by Him to be cared for within reasonable limits, and that the pleasures of Earth are not to be despised since they also are His Gift, and meet for man’s enjoyment. ‘True pleasures of the earth planet are an earnest of the delights of Paradise. I have digressed somewhat in order to make my meaning clear to you, for such a belief was not a part of my philosophy in earth-life. The Neophyte, therefore, finding the trend of the Divine within, will find himself in natural opposition to evil forces, and will, indeed, have much ado to combat them, since Matter, at the present time, has much degenerated, and the conflicting powers are much augmented by the strength of their ever increasing numbers. Blindly they are working backwards toward the upward gradation of the Cycle, but in the direction which leads to Oblivion. O Neophyte, affrighted by opposing Power, dismayed by the darkness, take heart, for here is thy gold tried in the furnace and from hence shall thy Spirit soar unscathed. Who shall deserve the Nirvana of God, who shall adore the Vision of the Eternal Son, who had not come victor from the conflict and won the Laurel Crown? I have written of the First Hours of the conscious Life of the Soul, when he has descended into the depths of Matter, and found the Lord God within himself, Light and Darkness within his own Soul. Behold now, the Neophyte must traverse beyond the presence of living Matter into which he is incarnated, into the extreme depth which is Inertia. Before there can be Resurrection, there must be Death, ere the Neophyte can commence his ascent into Nirvana he must plumb the extremities of the lowest Arc of the Cycle of Creation. He must dare the darkness of the Hells, and the furnace that shall destroy his fixed nature, that his conscious spirit may arise from the ashes fit for ascent into the Region of the Blessed. It is not with this aspect of the matter I am here concerned, but, rather, with the potentialities of the Spirit while still occupying its fleshly body and manifesting in Matter. This, at the present time, is of paramount importance, since we have the Heavenly Hosts over here, discarnate, but only by re-incarnation into matter can they become articulate to Man, and this indeed is an agonizing work for one advanced in Spirit Life, to return and suffer over again the tribulations of Earth. The Initiate, therefore, who is willing to brave the forces of the elements, to probe Matter even to its lowest potential aspect which is inertia, to make the Sacrifice of himself as an Ego, that his being may be absorbed into the mysteries to which he penetrates and that he may be imbued with understanding, acquires, by this his oblation, a divine Wisdom that has lightened Mankind in ages now gone by, and shall enlighten them again in the ages yet to come. In our day, that is, when I incarnated upon Earth, we worked in a world that was much given to pleasure and debauchery, and though Art and wisdom were, perhaps, at a flood-tide on your globe, yet we lacked much that is inspiration to you now. ‘The Jews looked for a Messiah, but this national expectancy was not of much moment to Mankind at large. It was only with our discarnation came the knowledge of a divine prophecy but newly fulfilled. The Divine Initiate, the Son of God, accomplished for you that same descent into Matter, that same

Ordeal by Fire, that Oblation by Himself once offered, that Sacrifice unto Death. This was the Fulfilment of Prophecy, the Climax of esoteric teaching, the Perfect Example of Initiation. *We, on earth, were forerunners, proclaiming a Master Who was Nameless and Unknown, you are the followers of a divine Leader, who shirked no iota of the Sacrifice, and is present with you now, guiding the aspirant toward his goal, inspiring all who will but submit themselves to His Leadership. His is not the Sacrifice that others might elude the exigencies of service. Not so humanity shall gain Nirvana. He suffered not that Man might exclude suffering from the gamut of his initiation, for thereby would man be greatly the loser. For himself must each initiate make the descent, and for their own misdeeds must Mankind suffer the penalty. It was because of their misdeeds there came the Son of God. I believe that even His contemporaries misunderstood the issues. It behoves me to consider how far I should digress in order to make the matter clearer. Philosophy, wisdom, nay, even religion in those days were in the hands of the learned—that which was given to the people was given in symbols, and to the many it was incomprehensible altogether. The subject of initiation was a matter for the sages. Healing arts were practised by magicians, humanity as a whole was aware of no Spiritual Presence inspiring their lives, no personal God Who was a Present Help, an Understanding Entity. To them came the Christ of God, the Divine * Philosophers of the Pythagorean School?

Initiate, demonstrating day by day among them that the true essence of all philosophy, of all wisdom, is within the mind—you would say the heart—of man, rather than relegated to his carnate intelligence. He lived the life of an Initiate, lived it openly in the market-place. The Sacrifice, wont to be offered within the secret places of the Temples of Egypt, He made upon the topmost heights of Calvary where all might see. He practised the Healing Arts in gentle simplicity, without potions or incantation, aye, and bade others do likewise as indeed they did, since you may read that His apostles followed Him in this. Ignorant fishermen of Galilee, they achieved that which had been the monopoly of the learned and the Mystic. Therefore, the Atonement promises you not exemption from the effects of error. Had He so atoned you would have lost the most potent of your means of progression. Nay, rather, He atoned for the fact of the presence of Sin upon the earth. Sin is spiritual darkness, and therefore it saith truly in your Book that God cannot look upon Sin. When all is dark, all is invisible. Therefore came the Light of the World, that by His light the world might be visible to spirit-eyes, and acceptable in the Sight of God. His pure Light counteracted, atoned for, the darkness, in order that help might be sent more freely among mankind. Thus the dual aspect of the Initiation of the Christ _—first, the Atonement of Light for the darkness, and secondly the divine Example of how man might atone for his error and attain his Heaven thereby.

Here we return to the Neophyte and to the meaning and the substance of the Fire through which he shall pass. The Initiate of Egypt, passing in his youth into the silences of the Temples, evoked artificial means of undergoing the test of fire. He submitted himself to many kinds of ordeals, many of them dangerous to his body and even to his life, many of them fraught with dangers to his spirit-body by reason of his deliberate projection of his Ego among the Spirit-Essences. He set himself to destroy his flesh as a detaining factor in his life, to overcome many of its natural exigencies and to deny its passions. He passed through the fires of ordeal that the volitions of his body might undergo death, and his spirit-self, untrammelled, rise to Nirvana. And, having once attained, a veil then separated the Initiate from the people. He stood alone, unapproachable, above them in experience and in wisdom. Nevertheless, each unit among the people was, and is, a potential Initiate. To each one, ignorant or learned, rich or poor, comes the same descent into Matter, the same manifestation of spirit within the flesh, the same ordeal in the melting-pot of life, the same destruction of their fixed nature, the same uplifting to those who overcome. I do not belittle the Initiate in this, his courage, his steadfastness, his faith, nor do I belittle his wisdom and his knowledge which can greatly benefit mankind, but among the beatitudes of Nirvana, I have learned that the people are not despised because the Initiate

is exalted. Some there are among the least of earth’s little lives who have passed through the terrors of a far more rigorous initiation than any undergone within the portals of the Temple, and are risen among the blessed of God. Herein I am unfolding to you the necessity for suffering upon the earth. The man who descends not those last steps of involution through Fire to Inertia, is static, stationary. He is not progressing toward the Divine Essences and the Spheres of Light. I speak of existence as a whole. A man may suffer more than one incarnation, and only once need he make the descent. I cannot make this quite clear to you, but it is certain that, during its existence, the Ego must touch that lowest point of the Arc, the Omega of the Universe. Only so he may rise, only so he is fitted to rise. On earth, your prizes are not given to those who reclined at ease while the race was run. The Neophyte, therefore, having discovered the Force that is within his nature, now learns its application to the elements. Surrounded by fire, he learns to control it, he learns to transmute the elements and to become the master of Matter of which himself, physically, he is a part. Force may destroy mass, and reduce substance to its elementals. The elementals may be re-assembled to form different substances. Knowledge, accumulated within the brain cells may inform man how this may be done within certain limits of space and variation, but it is only the Mind of Man, the spiritual Force within his Ego, that shall control the Elements. The chemist shall not hold burning coals upon his palm and remain unscorched, but the Psychic may do it. From the unknown past it has been done by the Initiates and regarded as a trick by the ignorant. All Matter is interpenetrated by Force, and the only Power that shall control it is the corresponding Force within the Mind of Man. That Life-Element is of God, Who has given to mankind control over Matter. The Master said: By faith ye may move mountains. What is faith? The World will say it is belief in this dogma or that. It is not so. Faith is the consciousness of the Life-Force, the immense potential Power within the Ego. This Force is linked with the Cosmos, with the Spiritual, with the Supreme, and as such, has supreme power over Matter, and more than this, it has the ability to draw upon the Infinite for replenishment. It would be dangerous, most dangerous, for man to realize this power in his present state of existence. Scientists are probing towards this discovery, but it will not be permitted to them until Man is fitted to receive it. At the present time, Man is greatly encompassed by evil. ‘This is not a necessary factor in this descent. The extreme point of Inertia to which he must reach, is Negative, it is the complete nullity of all Force, it is the inertia of Matter when the Force within the Atom has been withdrawn from it, but it is not of necessity evil.

CHRIST THE INITIATE It is those who have failed in the first hours of their initiation, who have turned back in self-seeking or cowardice and opposed themselves to the current of Eternal Love which flows through Involution to Evolution, it is these who have permeated these conditions with evil. Until this condition is remedied, Man must, for his own sake, remain ignorant, or he would destroy himself and the Matter in which he functions. Yet because of this necessity, it behoves it not that the Initiate who had attained to a greater knowledge should not seek to enhance the power within himself. Nay, for this he should strive the harder, for whether he will or no, and whatever walk of life he may be in, the Staff of the Pastor is given him, and he it is who shall lead the flock. That which science shall not discover yet, the Mind of the Individual may discover for himself, and he shall become a superman. Arcazaiel.

The power is ever held in check, both in the auric spheres of earth and in the mind of the individual. Once Mankind, in unit or in mass, withdraws his volition, then the evil emanations which contact with him are unable to draw further nourishment, when they are rendered negative by spiritual reaction, and fall into Inertia or Death. Therefore nought but that which is wholly evil shall undergo the Second Death, of which wrote the Apostle John. Nought but that which is evil shall become inert or be destroyed. God is Life, therefore that which is of God shall endure. The last downward step of the Neophyte in involution is at one with the turning-point where he sets his face towards the Divine. At one hour with Death is also the Resurrection and the Life. Fear not that vortex which is the melting-pot, for verily that which is Divine shall arise therefrom unscathed. At physical death, the Soul of Man shall arise, comparatively through degrees of progression, while his body, comparatively inert, in reality analogous to the Earth from which it was evolved, shall return to the earth, as all Matter, having affinity, must reassemble. At the Second Death, evil shall perish in absolute nullity, and the Soul be received into the State of Absolute Good, the Nirvana of God. Oh foolish generation which insists that this and this is of chemical extraction, and this and this emotional !

The secretions of the glands affect not only the body but the character of a man. They are able to give prolonged youth and to impinge upon his mental tendencies. Whence come these secretions? They may be treated from without, a fact which alone proves man may not suffer eternal judgement upon the evidence of a physical existence in which he had control only of the partial consciousness which has its limits within the cortex of a human brain. The glands are also, per contra, affected by the emotions. What are the emotions? ‘The impinging of higher chemical Agencies upon the Life-Force or Mind of Man. It will doubtless come as a shock to some that I should speak of a religious inspiration, among others, as a chemical agency. This I will explain. Contact with Higher Powers reaches the Mind and through the Mind, the brain, as a thought. Thought is definitely chemical in its action, not on the physical plane of chemistry but upon the mental and astral through which it contacts gradually with slower vibrations through the intermediate states. Why say you there is oxygen in a man’s lungs? You cannot see it. You cannot smell it. Yet your researches have proved its presence. At one time your researches had not arrived at this point of achievement. Then why deny the existence of other elements within that elaborate organism, the body of man?
Why blind yourselves to all that is out of reach?

Each year brings its own discoveries. Why deny that which is not proven? Martyrs have been sacrificed upon the altar of Knowledge as well as upon the altar of Religion, and the years have acquitted them.

He is ready to seek those lands with their conditions, their climate, which lie beyond the etheric fields and out of reach of his imagining. Behold, our face is set upward toward the skies. Rightly man looks upward, outward from the Earth plane, for the Spirit-World exists in ever-widening spheres beyond the confines of the aura of Earth. These spheres widen ever, becoming inter-planetary and eventually inter-solar. Yet, even this fact is a matter of condition as much as of geography. Not only is there space in the Heavens for the astral body, but space for the Mind, where those qualities in man which are beautiful shall enlarge unceasingly. There is no definite spirit-body that Man shall assume once and for all at “ death.”’ Man’s nature is not dual, but threefold, in relation to physical conditions. The primary element is the Prana, or LifeElement. This develops around itself a mental condition, built up of definite elements undistinguishable by yourselves, but known to you as the Ego, or Subconscious Self. ‘This Ego incarnates into the physical, and the physical and mental personalities grow together under carnate conditions. The Nucleus of the Ego, the Life-Force, is not subject to growth, being in Itself perfect, but only to individualizing consciousness. At “ death ” the physical body reverts to the earth which bred it, and the mental state of the entity incarnates, or manifests, in such material as is suited to its development. ‘This may be astral matter, as is

sometimes the case with earth-bound spirits, which accounts for their frequent visibility to those still incarnate. Others assume the substance of higher and yet higher Planes. They may, on the other hand, descend into darker, or lower, states, in which case the material available to them for manifestation will be of a very low order. In every instance the Mind, or Ego, will imitate automatically the appearance of the physical body as it appeared during earth-life. The appearance of personality will be identical, yet greatly enhanced or modified by the quality of the material taken from the Plane of its new residence and used for this new incarnation into individual spirit-life. Those Egos which assume an astral body, will have, to you, the most normal appearance, since their new forms will have been assembled of material more nearly analogous to Earth. ‘Those dark spirits who seek the haunts of evil will be enabled out of those vicious and corroding chemicals there available, to build themselves an ugly and contorted body, which shall truthfully and justly depict the darkness of their own mental nature. These poor souls are subject to progression. With the destruction of the evil within their minds, with the _ withdrawal of the evil volitions on which evil matters feed, comes the corresponding decomposition of their contorted bodies. So, with the dawn of beauty and goodness within their minds comes the assumption of a new etheric or mental body corresponding to their new mental attitude, and analogous to the Plane to which their new condition brings them automatically. From this point there is no hindrance to their progress. There are none eternally damned. Could that Spark of Eternal Life, proceeding from the Father, be subject to oblivion? No. Yet a man may give much of his mental Ego and his conscious power to evil, in which case much is lost to him and suffers destruction. That which a man gives of himself for good, whether it be in act or thought or emotion, that shall be his for eternity, but that which is evil shall persist a little while, and then be no more, for this very reason, that the condition upon which it lives is relative, and conditional only upon the perversion of the Forces which, in essence, are altogether good. Evil exists upon the very Power that must destroy it. Yet for a while, it lives and the vengeance it would wreak fails in its purpose, and because of its integral Good, it begets in Man those traits which he could in no other way have attained, courage, long-suffering, sympathy, and, in so much greater a measure than else were possible—Love. ND now, by contrast, the state to which the spirit shall ascend who is purified and strengthened, shall not be less analogous to earth conditions outwardly, but as such forms as I have described were debased, so by contrast shall these be greatly enhanced in beauty. The aspect of the spirit-body shall in no way have lost its facial characteristics, its manners, its personality. Rather shall these be enhanced, since the mental attitude and the etheric waves of thought are able to react upon it. It must be remembered that this form is but a spirit-body only in a relative sense. It is actually Matter, this also in a relative sense, which clothes the spirit which has as yet only commenced its ascent and has not regained the true Spirit-World. That which is known to you as the spirit-body is spiritual in relation to the material conditions prevailing on earth. It is a far higher form of expression. It is, nevertheless, a chemical production though the $2

chemical elements which compose it are of an entirely different order from any of those known to you. They are analogous to material elements and are interpenetrated in the same manner by the more purely spiritual. All the elements forming this body correspond to their environment. ‘They are withdrawn from a particular Spirit-Sphere, or Cycle, for this purpose, in order that the Spirit or Ego may be tangible and able to manifest normally in this Sphere of activity for which his nature is suited. ‘This is parallel with his earth incarnation with this outstanding difference. Upon the earth planet Matter is so gross that it is not easily manipulated, and the only manner in which the Spirit can incarnate is by means of the parental protoplasm which alone is sufficiently mobile andsympathetic for the purpose. In this manner the Ego can gather atomic Matter and is able to assimilate the chemicals necessary to its growth through the channels of the maternal frame. Once replete with sufficient strength and instinct it seeks independent existence and lives thenceforth by extracting chemicals from its food, assimilated within the body, as well as from the ether drawn into the body from without by means of the lungs and the dermal pores. During this process of development known to you as Life, a parallel process is taking place. ‘The magnetism within the body, generated by the Life-Force or Spirit, is absorbing from the environing Atoms Cosmic Power and evolving what is known to you as an *etheric double.” Thus the purpose of its descent into Matter is twofold, although the functioning of these two aspects of the same form are so closely interwoven that, in our eyes, the experience is considered as a whole. The relation of the physical body to the etheric body isas the cornea to the eye or the tympanum to the ear. It is the vehicle used for the reception of experience. I wish to emphasize this definition. Every possible tinge of feeling, whether registered by the physical brain or not, is received into the Subconscious Mind, or etheric double of the individual. The embryo of this etheric mind is infinitely older than the physical body since it has been built up around the integral Spirit ever since its first outset from the Spirit-State. At first, all that it gathered was rare and holy because its downward journey had but commenced and it was still passing through the Supreme Altitudes. With the graduations of its descent so the atomic Matter which it was able to absorb from its environment became of a grosser nature. It is manifest therefore, that the formation of man, fundamentally, corresponds to the formation of the earth or other forms of Matter, that is, it is built up of spherical strata imposed one upon the other. First, the Principle of Life, around which is gathered a stratum, or sphere, of divine Substance, which is in turn surrounded by other and larger spheres imposed one upon the other, each increasingly dense in substance. ‘This process continues until the incarnating Ego has reached the planes which exist within the radius of our knowledge. Upon these strata of spiritconditions he gathers other states, he acquires Matter

from the mental, astral and etheric planes respectively and, thus fortified and prepared, enters the material state and becomes carnate and tangible upon the earth plane. Henceforth, every reaction undergone by the physical body, whether the experience be received through the senses or more directly from etheric contact, is registered upon his “ etheric double ”’ which is the next stratum of his integral self. From thence it penetrates through the spheres of his Being, modified by the nature of his composition, until it reaches the abode of his Spirit. Thus the entity attains to conscious individuality and becomes a separate Unit in the Scheme of Creation. Now, therefore, the shedding of the physical body at death, is to the individual as the paring of an onion skin. As this vegetable retains its shape and general appearance after this simple operation, so does the individual. The determining factor is this, in what condition shall the under-skin be found? We will leave on one side all conditions of positive evil, since with this aspect I have dealt already. We will consider here the varying grades of evolution to which the entity is subject. The carnate body, the outer scale, is shed. The outer sphere, or conscious self of the individual, is now the Astral State. If he desires still to mingle with earth conditions he will retain this body and will strengthen it with atomic matter obtained from the astral plane. In order to do this, he will not be obliged to suffer any process of incarnation, since Matter, here being less gross in nature, will respond to his natural powers of attraction, and he will find himself articulate upon a plane which corresponds to his new state. ‘To be precise, he will find himself in a world which gives him the same aspect of solidity as did the earth plane, his body will retain all its imprint of personality and appear normal, though slightly enhanced in beauty.

In this condition he will be enabled to hold converse with will those who be enabled are sympathetic to his own state, he to return to earth and to glean much information of earth’s happenings through normal observation. The atomic composition of material matter will now be more apparent to him, and for this reason illusion all forms will assume an altered of solidity will be impaired by aspect, and the the first gleams of Truth which come down to him through the
Spirit-Spheres to which he has drawn nearer by this one step.

His spiritual body is left far back in the Spheres, even as his earth-body has been left in the world of flesh. He is naked, and fit to be arrayed in the Garments of the Antechambers of Heaven. He is now within the Light, but he beholds it not, for beholding it, he would be blinded and singed and burned. A man may not enter a room to face the violet ray without protection for his flesh and eyesight. Thus they who dwell in the heights welcome the Magus at the Portals of the Divine and lead him whither he may be clad in raiment that shall clothe his soul and protect it until such time as he be so far progressed that he may behold It without hurt. The Magus may now survey himself. He has known the body of flesh, and beheld its personalities still intact in the Spirit-form that was his in the Astral Spheres. ‘There, he beheld it transluscent, radiant, healthful. Clad he was in garments corresponding nearly with those of earth during the periods you have come to know as “ classic,’’ and enlivened with precious stones not unlike those for which you mine to-day. ‘This was rebirth indeed, and Resurrection, but he beholds now a greater Phenomenon. The imprint of his personality remains to him, is in fact, enhanced, but his body has ceased to be organic, as you recognize organism. His form is now electrical in nature, constructed with all necessary mechanism for absorbing the Magnetism that constitutes the aerial substance as oxygen and its like constitute your own. The Magnetism is indrawn through the receptive faculty of the body and expelled in individualized creative force. The Whole is thus drawn upon to create the Specific.

His new garments do not serve to conceal his dazzling personal beauty, but he is vaguely aware of that which he shall know of a certainty later on, that they are woven of especial purpose, and that henceforth he may assume them at will when he cometh to these Courts, for their virtue is of the Plane to which he has come and their potency shall be the insulator that shall serve to render the Ecstatic Vision endurable to him, and enable him to walk in the full effulgence of the Sunlight.
He is enshrouded therefore, and only from within the intangible folds of that gracious mantle may he behold the Unseen.
O, how explain these Glories to you earth-born spirits? How describe the sweet cadences of music to him who is born deaf?
I stumble to find words, and you are deaf to hear, for here we stand at the Courts of the Holy One of God.
Before that Sublime moment when the Portals shall be thrown apart, I will make one more digression.
There are those who have written from the

Spirit-Spheres and described Visions of the Christ. In many phases of experience He has walked among men. Yea, but in these Visions the Christ has come to Man, not Man to the Christ. In these ecstatic moments Man has beheld Him only as he himself could bear to see Him. He Who was made Man, is able to assume whatsoever outward Form He will. Yet even so, such occasion is very rare, and only the dire need of a soul most highly attuned to His Love, or the greatest ecstasy of adoration can bring Him so through the intervening spheres. Most often He cometh in Vision, in such manner as you would describe as a thought-form, where will and action and knowledge are present while the actual Entity functions elsewhere. But the Magus who has sought Nirvana through succeeding stages of Initiation is permitted to enter within the Portal of the Christ-Spheres, even as Saint John was permitted to enter, and behold the Christ in True Splendour. One question more you ask : How could the Initiate of Egypt behold the Christ two thousand years and more before Jesus dwelt in Galilee? My answer is a simple one: Because the Christ was not manifest to you in flesh was no argument that He existed not. His manifestation through Jesus of Nazareth was an Incident. ‘The greatest Incident in the history of your earth, yes, but it still remained but three-and-thirty solar years out of Eternal Life, The Jews rejected the Christ not because they did not believe in God, but because they could not recognize God in human form.

For many centuries the earth had worshipped God the Creator. That in some Form He could be partially visible to man they knew, since He had manifested to Moses and Elijah and to many of the Initiates.
The extent of the Cosmos was known still less than it is known to-day, and the existence of a Godhead beyond all human knowledge, all Form, all Time, all
Space, was beyond the imagination of that day. Yet the Father of All, of Whom we know nought at all except He be the Author of Cosmic Creation, the
_ Fountain Head of all Light, Goodness and Existence, | vouchsafed us One Who might manifest Him within range of human conception. This Manifestation of

God, Man called “God” and rightly so, yet there exists a distinction, for God Himself is Unseen, Unapproachable, and He Who manifests Him has taken a Form by which we may perceive Him. It is this Form, this Manifestation, of which mankind has been aware throughout all ages, that is known in Heaven as The Christ.

Therefore I say that the Manifestation of this Divine Spirit in Jesus of Nazareth was an Incident. It was much more than this, but I accentuate it because the nature of that Incarnation has been much misunderstood.
This was a human body, humanly born. Verily God took our nature upon Him. In all ways He functioned through our nature during the course of His

earth-life. Therefore He said, “‘ That which I do ye also can do.” It is admitted that some change took place in the manner in which mankind regarded the Christ after this stupendous Event. They learned a very tender personal Love toward Him Whom they had feared. ‘They knew God not only as their Creator, but as their Redeemer. They were content to beae God through this Form made manifest to them. That which lies Beyond is known to Him alone. | What is within the Divine, the Infinite, we may not know. ‘Through the Ages, perchance, He may lead us onward to a greater knowledge and still more vast, unfolding World. It is beyond our conception now, | and we desire it not, save in His good time. For the present, we can conceive no joy more ecstatic, — no splendour more effulgent, than the proximity of | Him Who once was Son of Man. This is the Light of the World, this is the Nucleus around which all known creation revolves. ‘Thus is the First Principle expounded, the great Axiom of cyclic revolutions around a superior Centre. Herein is the highest Form we know of that Principle which animates all Matter down to the formation of the Atom and even of atomic particles. _ The units in all cases revolve around their centre by reason of their attraction to it, this affinity being in itself a manifestation of the Magnetic Love Stream which permeates the Cosmos. Also is it an immutable Law that the Nucleus is not fixed, but is itself an electron in a larger sphere of activity. Therefore it is our belief that even this Sublime Centre of Holiness may itself be a Sun in the Eternal Orbit of the Father God.

The Holy Christ of God inspired and manifested in the Man Jesus, but the Light of Heaven went not out, nor was lessened because its Source sojourned awhile within one obscure planet. The Christ could not be contained wholly in Jesus. Jesus might be, and but was, wholly God, for a whole not a part the whole.

Theirs is that precious inheritance of personal love which some of us who adored from afar off wait long years to attain. Behold now the Supreme Ecstasy, but behold with eyes still veiled. The Spirit pervades all Creation, this is Life, the Prana, the Universal Magnetism, the Primal Force which invades every Atom, and, by attraction of qualities, links together all Matter, all Mass, and unites all Motion into one Purpose. Behold now this Divine Spirit manifest in the form of Man. It is said that every man, purified, is a Manifestation of God, and so he is, but even so, his consciousness is limited to the extent of his experience. The individuality of his Ego is newly fledged. He is able to draw upon cosmic power for life and wisdom, but he himself is not a source of power except in a local and restricted sense. ‘The consciousness of Man is potentially infinite only because it is linked with the Divine Consciousness, and he is himself Divine potentially because he sprang from holy Origin. His individuality is the outcome of a free-will that has been moulded within the Will of God.
